title: IOM survey finds more than 7.1 million people internally displaced in Ukraine
body:
On 5 April 2022, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported that more than 7.1 million people had been internally displaced in Ukraine since the Russian invasion began on 24 February 2022. The figure came from the second round of IOM's General Population Survey, conducted between 24 March and 1 April 2022, and was 10 percent higher than the estimate from the first round on 16 March 2022.

The survey described the composition of displaced households. More than half of them included children, 57 percent included elderly members and 30 percent included people with chronic illnesses. Household incomes fell sharply: the share of displaced households earning less than 5,000 hryvnias (about 170 US dollars) per month rose from 13 percent before 24 February to 61 percent after the war began, and more than a third of displaced households reported having no income in the previous month.

IOM reported that the most pressing needs were cash and financial support, transportation, food, shelter and hygiene items, with medicines and health services ranking second for both displaced people and those who had stayed in their homes. The organisation said it was providing food, non-food items, hygiene supplies, cash, mental health and psychosocial support and information campaigns against trafficking and exploitation. IOM called for humanitarian corridors to allow the safe evacuation of civilians and for a cessation of hostilities to allow access to affected populations.
